features.name: Roux Solver: First Block
features.description: Generate a human-style move sequence that builds the left 1x2x3 block (FB). No Kociemba output
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: src/lib/solver/ (pieces.ts, search.ts, firstBlock.ts). solveFirstBlock(state) builds FB the Roux way and returns named steps: optional whole-cube rotation (orange left, yellow down), the yellow-orange DL edge, then for each corner-edge pair (shorter order first): free the pieces if stuck on the left side, join corner and edge using only U/R/r/M (never touch the left side), insert the joined pair with face turns while it stays joined every move. Each phase is as short as possible (IDA* over tracked pieces with distance tables); ties go to the easiest moves (moveEffort). No Kociemba. Random cubes: ~9.9 moves on average (vs ~9.2 for plain shortest steps), max 15 over 300; median 0.6ms, first solve ~250ms (builds tables). ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 149/149 tests incl. 15 new: move tables match cubejs for all 24 search moves; 100 seeded scrambles check every phase (free leaves both pieces reachable, join uses only U/R/r/M and ends joined, insert keeps the pair joined on every move, DL edge and finished pairs stay home after each step); exact free/join/insert for F' U R U' F; rotated and M-offset cubes start with a rotation; next build). Revised after owner review: the first version solved each pair as a plain shortest search, which didn't teach pairing. Not wired into /tutor yet: the demo lesson stays hand-written until SB/CMLL/LSE exist.

features.name: Roux Solver: Second Block
features.description: Build the right 1x2x3 block using only R, r, U, and M moves
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: src/lib/solver/secondBlock.ts. solveSecondBlock(state) builds SB the Roux way from a cube whose first block is solved, using only R, r, U and M (so the first block is never touched), and returns named steps: the yellow-red DR edge, then for each right pair (shorter order first): free the pieces if stuck in a right-side slot, join corner and edge in the top layer, insert the joined pair while it stays joined every move. The DR edge and finished pairs are home at the end of every phase. A step never starts on the layer the previous step ended on (no 'R2' then 'R''). Same IDA* search and moveEffort tie-breaks as FB. M-slice centers are left turned (LSE fixes them); the DR-edge step says so when they are off. Also isSecondBlockSolved (right center + 5 pieces) and solveBlocks (FB then SB). Random cubes (400): SB 15.0 moves on average, max 21 (plain per-piece shortest would be ~13.3); first solve ~60ms (builds tables), then median 1.6ms, max 12ms; FB unchanged (~170ms first, 0.5ms median). 2000 random-state cubes: all solved, max 23. ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 162/162 tests incl. 13 new in secondBlock.test.ts: 120 seeded scrambles check every move is R/r/U/M, the first block stays solved after every move, free ends with the pair out of the slots, join ends joined in the top layer, insert keeps the pair joined every move, DR edge and finished pairs home after each step; exact cases R2, R U R', R U' R' (join M, insert r U R'), free/join/insert and free-then-insert; after FB+SB only top corners, the 6 LSE edges and M centers are unsolved; next build). Not wired into /tutor yet.

features.name: Roux Solver: CMLL
features.description: Recognize the top-layer corner case and apply the matching CMLL algorithm
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: src/lib/solver/cmllCases.ts (table) and cmll.ts (solver). 42 CMLL algorithms in the usual 8 sets (O 2, H 4, Pi 6, U 6, T 6, S 6, AS 6, L 6), stored as data { id (e.g. 't-1', 'o-adjacent'), set, name ('T 1', 'O Adjacent'), nickname (Sune, Anti-Sune, Jb perm), alg, moves, recognition }. Algorithms written from common CMLL sheets, then checked by computer: 40 were right as remembered; H 3 actually solved a Pi case (replaced with R U2 R2 F R F' U2 R' F R F') and S 4 broke the second block (replaced with F R' U2 R F' R' F U2 F' R, found by a block-keeping search). Recognition is from the corners relative to the blocks only (never the top center): a lookup over all 647 unsolved top-corner states gives the shortest pre-AUF + algorithm + post-AUF, worked out by undoing each option on a solved cube. Recognition notes are generated from each case (where the top color faces, bar/opposite/neighboring colors per side, plus cross-side sticker comparisons until the case can't be confused with any other) and the table build throws if two cases look alike. solveCmll(state) returns steps cmll-pre-auf (U turn, optional), cmll (name like 'CMLL: Sune case (S 1)', goal with the set shape and recognition note, step.case = the case), cmll-post-auf (optional; ends with corners solved relative to the blocks). Also isCmllSolved, solveThroughCmll (FB + SB + CMLL). 1000 random-state cubes: CMLL 11.3 moves on average (algorithm 9.8 + AUFs), max 17; first call ~40ms (builds the table), then median 0.02ms, max ~1ms. ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 182/182 tests incl. 20 new: every algorithm keeps both blocks and the L/R centers, uses no rotations, solves its case also with the middle slice turned and belongs to the set its twists say; the 42 algorithms solve 42 different cases; all 648 top-corner states (with the middle slice turned on 3 of 4) end with corners solved and blocks intact, using the fewest moves the table allows, all 42 cases used; 120 seeded scrambles through FB + SB + CMLL; exact Sune, pre-AUF, post-AUF, skip and O Adjacent cases; next build). Not wired into /tutor yet.

features.name: Roux Solver: LSE
features.description: Solve the last six edges using only U and M moves (EO, UL/UR, EP)
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: src/lib/solver/lse.ts (LSE) and roux.ts (full chain). solveLse(state, { previousMove? }) solves a cube whose blocks and top corners are solved (top layer may be turned) with U and M only, in three human Roux phases: lse-eo (all six edges good; case by bad edges: eo-1-1, eo-2-0-adjacent|opposite, eo-0-2, eo-3-1 'arrow', eo-4-0, eo-2-2-adjacent|opposite, eo-6-flip), lse-ulur (white-orange and white-red edges between their own corners, top layer lined up or a half turn off; cases ulur-top-auf, ulur-both-top, ulur-top-bottom, ulur-both-bottom), lse-ep (last four edges + centers + final top-layer turn; cases ep-centers, ep-3-cycle-uf|df|db|ub, ep-swap-front-back|top-bottom|diagonal, judged relative to the centers). After EO no move makes an edge bad again (a quarter U turn only while the white/yellow centers are up/down). Each step has id, name ('Orient edges: arrow (3 bad on top, 1 on the bottom)'), goal (includes the case's recognition text), moves, case { id, name, recognition }, centersOff (M turns the centers are off at the step's start). Distance tables over the whole LSE space (184,320 states, 5,760 with all edges good; ~30-50ms to build on first call) make every phase as short as possible; ties go to the plan with the shortest later phases, then no step starting on the layer the previous one ended on, then easiest moves. Also isLseSolved (every piece and center home, standard orientation) and lseBadEdges. solveRoux(state) -> { moves, stages: [fb, sb, cmll, lse] each { stage, moves, steps } }; in the chain CMLL's last top-layer turn (cmll-post-auf) is left to LSE when that is not longer (saves ~0.9 moves on average, same-layer starts between CMLL and LSE drop from ~25% to ~1.4%). 1000 random-state cubes (cubejs Cube.random): full solve 48.1 moves average (FB 9.9, SB 15.1, CMLL 10.8, LSE 12.4), max 61; LSE max 18; LSE median 0.05ms, max 1.2ms; full solve median 3ms (first ~280ms, FB tables); LSE started with the middle slice turned on 77%. Random LSE states: 11.2 moves average. ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 204/204 tests incl. 22 new: state-space counts and every phase finishable from every state; all 5,760 oriented states and all 32 flip patterns x 180 sampled states (5,760 more) solved with every phase checked move by move on the real cube; 3,000 random LSE states; exact arrow, 1-1, 4-0 with the slice off, U-perm-like 3-cycle, M2 U2 M2 U2, centers-only, AUF and previous-move cases; 120 seeded scrambles with slice/wide turns through solveRoux end solved, mapped onto createLesson; next build). Not wired into /tutor yet.

features.name: Move Explanations
features.description: Every move in the solve maps to a dictionary entry explaining why it is played; shown in the drawer as the user steps through
features.evidence: 2026-10-28: src/lib/tutor/explanations.ts: EXPLANATIONS, a dictionary of 79 templates (68 specific + 11 per-step '.other' fallbacks) keyed '<stage>.<step>.<what the move does>' (e.g. fb.join.final, sb.insert.open, cmll.alg.breaks, lse.eo.flip, lse.ulur.spot), and explainRouxSolution(start, solveRoux(start)), which plays the solve and picks each move's entry from its stage, step id, CMLL/LSE case and what the move does on the cube (which pair piece it moves, joins, lifts or puts back finished pieces, slots the pair, opens the slot, starts/ends/breaks/restores in an algorithm, flips edges, brings UL/UR edges up, etc.), then fills piece colors, positions, case names and moves left. Purpose claims that depend on later moves are checked against them (e.g. 'the next M turn brings the white-orange edge in'). /tutor now shows the Roux solver's solve of a fixed scramble (src/lib/tutor/demoLesson.ts + rouxLesson.ts), computed in the Server Component while the page prerenders at build time: no solver code in the browser (checked .next/static), /tutor still static, HTML 23KB / RSC 18KB. The drawer shows the move, the step's name and moves, the move's explanation, and the step goal behind an inline 'About this step' toggle; the content area scrolls with a CSS scroll shadow when it doesn't fit. ./init.sh passed (npm ci, typecheck, lint, 215/215 tests incl. 11 new: every move of 240 seeded random solves (with slice/wide turns and rotations, >10,000 moves) gets a non-fallback entry led by its move, <= 240 chars, all main entries used; listed bad edges match lseBadEdges; exact demo texts (back pair freed, front pair joined by R' naming yellow-green-orange + green-orange, Anti-Sune pre-turn and algorithm, arrow EO); exact R U R', R U' R', Sune, EO flip, EP and rotation cases; demo lesson = solveRoux output, each stage completes its pieces; TutorScreen shows/updates the explanation, step name and goal on Next/Back and plays the demo lesson to solved; next build). Ad hoc: 20,000 random-state cubes, no fallback entry used; explanation length median 108, p99 199 chars. Playwright on next start (390x844, 375x667, 320x568; light and dark): sheet top at 60%, no horizontal or page scroll, all 47 moves show distinct explanations, Back/Next always in view (64px, 56px under 700px tall), text fits on 44/47 moves at 390x844 and scrolls inside the sheet on smaller screens, goal toggle keeps the sheet at 60%, no console errors. No 'New scramble' button (see progress.md).

features.name: Camera Scanner
features.description: Live camera scan: the user turns the cube in front of the rear camera and each side is captured automatically when held steady inside a square guide (any order, tap a side to rescan). Centers identify the sides and calibrate the colors; the scanner works out each side's rotation from cube legality, then hands off to Manual Facelet Entry for correction
features.evidence: 2026-10-30: /scan (src/lib/scan/, src/components/scan/CubeScanner.tsx). Live scan: rear camera, guide square, a side is captured after ~0.5s held steady, any order and rotation, tap a thumbnail to redo; all 6 open /enter?cube=<draft>. Plain TypeScript (no OpenCV): 3x3 grid fit on a 120x120 snapshot (~28ms), colors learned from the scan's centers with exactly 9 per color, each side's rotation found from cube legality, leftover ambiguity left blank. ./init.sh passed (typecheck, lint, 274/274 tests incl. 27 new, next build with /scan static). Unit tests on synthetic sides (offset, size, tilt, stickerless, white plastic, glare, thumb, dim) and 60 random cubes under 4 lightings; Playwright with Chromium's fake camera playing generated videos of a scrambled cube (normal, and stickerless + warm light + smaller): exact cube in the editor, Ready to solve, at 390x844, 375x667 dark, 320x568, no page scroll, no console errors. Not yet tried with a real phone and cube. 2026-11-01: first real-phone scan captured one side 3 times; fixed in tracker.ts (lighting-tolerant same-side check, capture lock survives blurry frames), 3 new tests, ./init.sh passed (321/321). Then: a side whose center matches a scanned one replaces it in place instead of being added, 4 new tests, ./init.sh passed (324/324). Then: grey first side fixed (1 s camera warm-up, all-colorless dim or low-contrast sides rejected), 2 new tests, ./init.sh passed (326/326).
